objectives.title: Solve planar 2R inverse kinematics
objectives.statement: For a declared planar 2R arm with joint limits: decide reachability, find both analytic elbow branches and report honest failure. Solutions are judged by forward-kinematics residual and constraints, not a single reference angle pair.
excludes: Spatial or redundant arms, orientation IK, dynamics, whole-topic mastery and automatic code evidence

objectives.title: Plan a triangular or trapezoidal time law
objectives.statement: One-axis rest-to-rest time law under speed and acceleration limits: type, phase times, samples, reversed and zero moves, longer durations, impossible requests, and a common duration for two synchronised joints
excludes: Jerk limits, torque or dynamics, multi-point or Cartesian paths, controller tracking, robot execution, whole-topic mastery and automatic code evidence

objectives.title: Update a finite localization belief
objectives.statement: Exact 1-D discrete Bayes (histogram) filter on a ring or walled corridor with a declared sensor table and noisy motion kernel: normalized posterior, sense-then-move loop, ambiguity from symmetric layouts and honest handling of an impossible reading; plus deterministic particle weights, effective sample size and systematic resampling given an explicit draw. Numerical toy only; no SLAM claim.
excludes: SLAM, continuous-state or Kalman filtering, random-draw convergence statistics, real sensors or simulators, whole-topic mastery and automatic code evidence

objectives.title: Run and check a declared linear Kalman predict/update
objectives.statement: For a declared scalar or 2-state constant-velocity linear-Gaussian model with one scalar measurement: compute prediction, innovation, gain and posterior covariance, fuse independent sensors sequentially and in batch information form, and read NIS with an explicit false-alarm policy. Results are judged against analytic and batch oracles, and a correlated-noise or model-mismatch counterexample is named rather than hidden.
excludes: EKF/UKF and nonlinear models, vector measurements, tuning or estimating Q and R, ensemble consistency statistics over random draws, correlated-noise handling, real sensors, timing and hardware, whole-topic mastery and automatic code evidence

objectives.title: Plan on a grid and check a shortcut
objectives.statement: Cost-optimal A* on a small declared 4- or 8-connected occupancy grid (step costs 1 and sqrt(2), stated no-corner-cutting rule), admissible versus inadmissible heuristics, honest unreachable and budget-exhausted reports, and an exact segment-versus-rectangle shortcut check including touching and thin walls.
excludes: RRT, PRM or other sampling-planner completeness claims
Arm or configuration-space planning
Dynamics, moving obstacles, simulator or hardware runs
Whole-topic planning mastery and automatic code evidence

objectives.title: Fit a declared first-order model and judge identifiability
objectives.statement: For a declared discrete first-order model y[k+1] = a y[k] + b u[k] on small synthetic logs: form the 2x2 normal equations and fit (a, b) by least squares, recover known parameters from noise-free data, score the fit on a held-out log, read the Gram-matrix condition number to classify a log as identifiable, weak or unidentifiable, estimate parameter standard deviations from the Gram matrix, and draw bounded uniform or log-uniform parameters from explicit draws. Results are judged against Cramer's-rule and residual-orthogonality oracles; low excitation is named and answered with a new log rather than hidden.
excludes: Nonlinear, delayed, multi-input or closed-loop identification, noise estimation and regularisation choices, random sampling statistics, physics-simulator identification, real robot logs, sim-to-real or hardware transfer claims, whole-topic mastery and automatic code evidence

objectives.title: Project, deproject and check a synthetic pinhole calibration
objectives.statement: For a declared ideal pinhole (no distortion) and a declared world-to-camera rigid transform: project and deproject with positive depth, reject zero, negative or behind-camera depth, report reprojection RMS, and fit fx, fy, cx, cy by two independent least-squares lines from known camera-frame points, judged on held-out views rather than the training views. Results are checked against closed-form and exact-rational oracles; a leakage or wrong-axes counterexample is named rather than hidden.
excludes: Real images, checkerboard or corner detection, lens distortion beyond the ideal pinhole, full Zhang calibration with unknown poses, PnP and pose estimation, stereo, rolling shutter, device calibration, hardware and automatic code evidence, whole-topic mastery

objectives.title: Check episodes and a behaviour-cloning baseline
objectives.statement: On tiny numerical episode data: name injected defects (non-increasing or gapped timestamps, length mismatch, NaN, out-of-range values, exact duplicates), find an action/observation time lag, split whole sessions with no leakage, fit a least-squares line a = w o + b on training episodes only, and compare its held-out MSE with a mean-action baseline, including how a leak flatters the number. Numerical toy only; no generalization claim.
excludes: Neural policies, LeRobot or real robot datasets, multi-dimensional observations, closed-loop rollout, generalization or statistical claims, whole-topic mastery and automatic code evidence

objectives.title: Trace a task state machine with a watchdog
objectives.statement: A deterministic mock pick-and-deliver state machine: guarded transitions with preconditions, a timestamp watchdog (stale observation stops motion and enters a hold state), cancel and fault handling, bounded retry and explicit recovery without blind re-entry, event-trace replay, and a no-motion-while-stale/cancelled/faulted trace invariant.
excludes: Hazard analysis, human safety review and safety certification
Real emergency stop, hardware, ROS or real-time timing
Behaviour-tree libraries and automatic hazard coverage claims
Whole-topic safety mastery and automatic code evidence

objectives.title: Check a two-pad friction grasp and read its contact trace
objectives.statement: For a rigid box held by two parallel pads with the same Coulomb friction, using g = 9.81 m/s^2 and a quasi-static vertical lift: decide the hold condition 2*mu*N >= m*(g + a), compute the safety factor, the minimum squeeze per pad, the largest holding acceleration or mass, and friction-cone membership of a pad force (closed cone, pulling pads outside). Run a threshold retention observer over a declared synthetic (cmd, fn, ft) trace and name its contact, slip, lost, empty and release events, then reason from a slip or hold reading to a changed mass or friction. Checked against closed-form and exact-rational oracles.
excludes: Physics-engine contact simulation, soft or deformable contacts, torsional or rolling friction, multi-finger or form-closure grasps, grasp planning, force-sensor noise and delay, real grippers, any claim that the observer works on hardware, whole-topic mastery

objectives.title: Apply tabular updates and report seed results
objectives.statement: On tiny numerical toys: one-step tabular Q-learning and SARSA updates with correct terminal versus time-limit bootstrapping, epsilon-greedy probabilities, discounted returns, an exact value-iteration reference on a declared deterministic MDP, a per-seed raw-result report (mean, sample standard deviation, standard error) and a declared reward-loophole check. Numerical toy only; no simulator training or significance claim.
excludes: Simulator training, deep or continuous-control RL, PPO or SAC, stochastic transitions, significance tests, human protocol review, whole-topic mastery and automatic code evidence

objectives.title: Read a URDF chain and look up transforms between frames
objectives.statement: For a small serial-chain URDF-like fragment given as text (revolute, prismatic and fixed joints with origin xyz/rpy and axis): find the root and the chain order independently of file order, validate the structure (single root, no cycles, defined links, one parent per link, non-zero axis), compute the base-to-link transform at given joint values with rpy = Rz Ry Rx and origin-then-motion, and the transform between two links (TF-style lookup). Results are judged against an independent hand-composed fixture chain and the planar L02 forward kinematics, and a joint-origin or frame error is traced through the joint axis in the base frame.
excludes: Meshes, inertial and collision tags, xacro, mimic and continuous joints, joint limits, branching trees, ROS 2 TF2 runtime, timestamps and interpolation, robot_state_publisher, visualisation, calibration of a real robot, whole-topic mastery and automatic code evidence

objectives.title: Specify and test a replay node core
objectives.statement: Frame, duplicate/out-of-order stamp, maximum-gap and reset policies of a ROS-free odometry node core replayed on a recorded message list: which messages are used, the intermediate poses, and the smallest message set that exposes a named fault
excludes: ROS 2 runtime, DDS, QoS, TF2, ROS or simulated clocks, launch files, a real robot, whole-topic mastery and automatic code evidence

objectives.title: Select a target and take a bounded visual-servo step
objectives.statement: For a declared synthetic pan/tilt pinhole camera and labelled synthetic detections: select the target by label, freshness, depth window and confidence (never by colour alone), compute the observed normalized image error and the exact pan/tilt projection, apply a per-axis saturated proportional command, cancel with zero command when no detection is valid, and count steps over a declared finite convergence suite. Results are checked against exact geometry, hand-computed anchors and independent re-implementations; the limits of a finite suite are named rather than hidden.
excludes: Real or rendered images, feature or object detection, full 6-DOF image-based servoing with an interaction matrix, camera latency, motor dynamics and backlash, physics simulation, real cameras or robots, hardware and automatic code evidence, whole-topic mastery

objectives.title: Steer a pure-pursuit follower and judge its trace
objectives.statement: Pure-pursuit path following on a declared polyline: lookahead point from the circle-segment intersection ahead of the robot (stated tie, goal and lost rules), curvature kappa = 2 y_L / d^2, speed and turn-rate saturation along the same arc, a closed-loop kinematic simulation with a declared step, and offline trace evaluation (cross-track error, strict corridor test, goal tolerance, time-out, corner clearance and verdict order).
excludes: Nav2, ROS controllers, planners or costmaps
Localization, TF timeouts or clock behaviour in a running system
Physics-simulator, changed-layout or real-robot runs
Controller tuning, dynamics, obstacle avoidance and replanning
Whole-topic nonlinear control mastery and automatic code evidence

objectives.title: Update a belief and check a conditional plan in every possible world
objectives.statement: On a declared finite symbolic toy: STRIPS-style preconditions and effects, belief updates after sensing, weighted posteriors, running a conditional plan in every possible world to find a counterexample, and a groundedness check. Exact enumeration only; no perception, language or LLM reasoning.
excludes: Perception or language grounding, LLM/VLM reasoning, continuous or geometric task-and-motion planning, simulators, stochastic sensors and POMDP solving, human review of open-ended interpretations, whole-topic mastery, cognition certification and automatic code evidence

objectives.title: Check a one-link pendulum model, its energy and a computed-torque law
objectives.statement: One rigid link with a declared model (mass, centre-of-mass distance, inertia, damping, gravity): pivot inertia, gravity torque, acceleration, energy, explicit, semi-implicit and RK4 steps with energy drift and step-size sensitivity, a model check from energy samples, and a computed-torque law with a torque limit, holding capability and the offset left by a wrong gravity parameter
excludes: Multi-link or coupled dynamics, contact, friction beyond viscous damping, motor or gearbox models, physics engines, hardware torque control, controller tuning or stability proofs, whole-topic mastery and automatic code evidence

objectives.title: Check a mock joint interface, trajectory validator and action client
objectives.statement: For a made-up 2-joint arm, entirely MOCK: apply a declared interface lifecycle (unconfigured, inactive, active, finalized; commands only when active) with joint position limits and per-cycle velocity limits and read back state; validate a time-stamped joint trajectory and name every rejection reason (names, order, times, position and velocity limits, start state); trace a follow-trajectory action client through accept, feedback, cancel races, strict timeout and final states from a declared event list; and check a straight joint-space segment against a box obstacle by dense exact subdivision (a sampling check, not a proof). Mock evidence stays mock.
excludes: ros2_control, controller manager, lifecycle nodes and real hardware interfaces
MoveIt planning, planning-scene services and real planners
Real controllers, drivers, tracking error, real-time timing guarantees and any hardware
Link geometry, self-collision, thin-obstacle guarantees, whole-topic mastery and automatic code evidence
